thread:
maria-support: Customer ACME (Tkt#INC-12345) ran into intermittent 500s on /v1/generate and high token latency. They also asked whether our audit logs include plaintext request payloads — they're worried about retention & KMS/HSM scope. Ping security + oncall.

oncall-bot: Alert: 3 errors/min for acme-prod on us-west-2 for model 'redwood-7b'.

jordan-sre: Can you paste a sample request id and time? We need traces and the user's API key (masked) to locate KV cache behavior.

maria-support: Request IDs: r_2026-03-15T14:21:09Z_a1b2c3, r_2026-03-15T14:22:45Z_f9e8d7. Errors show `timeout writing response` in logs.

alex-infra: I'll pull traces. Initial hunch: GC+network flapping on node pool x-dedicated-3. Repro steps pls.

maria-support: Repro steps customer provided:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"<large prompt>","max_tokens":10240}'
2) they see 500 after ~18-25s
3) token billing jump observed in billing UI
Their payloads include compressed customer data.

sachin-security: Thanks. Important Q: are audit logs storing full request bodies or only metadata? If bodies are logged, KMS/HSM scope matters.

alex-infra: Confirmed logs have bodies in our request ingestion pipeline for debugging for spans older than 7 days (configurable). For hosted customers we redact keys but not necessarily payloads. That's controlled by `LOG_PAYLOADS` per-tenant flag.

lisa-legal: :warning: If payloads contain PII, we need to evaluate notification obligations. Who's the data owner at Acme? Also timeline for any retention beyond SLA.

jordan-sre: Quick check: show me the ingestion policy for acme-prod and whether `LOG_PAYLOADS` was true during the incident window.

alex-infra: Fetching... (gives snippet)
```json
{"tenant":"acme-prod","LOG_PAYLOADS":true,"retention_days":30,"log_sink":"audits-plain"}
```

sachin-security: If that's true, then KMS was used to encrypt logs at rest but HSM-wrapped keys? Need to confirm KMS key ARN and rotation status. Also check whether logs were exported to S3 bucket with public access — that's higher severity.

maria-support: Customer asking if we will notify affected users. They want an ETA for a formal response.

lisa-legal: We should prepare a customer-facing timeline. Suggest: acknowledge within 24h, provide initial findings within 72h, and remediation plan in 7 business days. Coordinating with security for scope.

alex-infra: I can confirm KMS ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01. Rotation last at 2025-11-02. No HSM wrap. Logs were not in public bucket — S3 ACLs private but object-level metadata indicates internal sharing to analytics team.

sachin-security: Flag: internal team access means more people could've viewed logs. We need access audit — who accessed logs between 2026-03-14 and 2026-03-16.

jordan-sre: I'll run an access audit query and paste results. If any non-service accounts show unusual access we'll escalate.

oncall-bot: Trace fetch completed: trace IDs t_acme_789,t_acme_790. Latency spike correlates with autoscaler churn timestamp 2026-03-15T14:20:30Z.

maria-support: Plan for customer reply: Confirm we're investigating, we found ingestion config that logged payloads for their tenant, we're auditing access and will follow notification timeline per legal. Assign owners: alex infra, sachin security, jordan SRE, lisa legal. @maria-support will draft.

lisa-legal: :thumbsup: I'll prep template and compliance checklist. If access audit shows only service accounts, low severity; if humans accessed payloads with PII then escalate to incident response.

maria-support: Thanks — I'll send the ack now. Keeping thread updated.
